title: Orchestrated degradation and staged eviction harness for asymmetric region partition
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: build an automated chaos harness that exercises an asymmetric region network partition combined with progressive GPU pool reclamation and dependent-service latency degradation. This test focuses on validating that tiered admission control, tenant-prioritized eviction, and circuit-breaker windows behave as intended under realistic drift (KV cache staleness, delayed 5xxs) while ensuring runbooks and alerting fire with actionable context. The harness should be reusable for canary runs and full-scale stress runs and produce artifactable traces, histograms, and a post-run summary for SLO regression detection.
acceptance_criteria: 1) The harness can simulate: control-plane partial egress loss in Region A, 30-70% GPU pool reclamation over 10 minutes, and a dependent-service blackhole that returns 500/502 with increasing latency jitter.
2) During the experiment, the platform maintains P99 latency SLOs for high-priority tenants where possible via staged shedding, and documents the trade-offs when lower-tier tenants are evicted.
3) Circuit breakers on the frontend and RPC layers trip with expected windows (configurable), and automatic fallback to smaller-capacity model variants occurs for supported routes.

4) Observability: traces contain a chaos-run id, token-level cost/latency tags, and a dedicated dashboard shows eviction counts, requeue rates, circuit breaker state transitions, and KV cache hit-rate drift.
5) Runbook triggers: when eviction rate > configured threshold or circuit-breaker open time > threshold, the runbook page is linked in the alert and a mitigation checklist is created automatically.
6) Post-run artifacts: a machine-readable summary (CSV/JSON) with per-tenant SLO violations, mean time to recovery of dependent services, and a short human summary is produced.
7) No customer data is exfiltrated; simulation uses synthetic traces and tenant masking to preserve privacy.
tasks: Design chaos scenarios matrix (region partition patterns, reclaim cadence, dep latency profiles)
Implement harness module to orchestrate: BGP/egress throttle emulation, GPU pool drain API, and dependency proxy that injects latency/5xxs
Add tenant-aware admission controller hooks to simulate prioritized eviction and throttling
Instrument runtime to emit chaos-run id, eviction_reason and tenant_priority labels into traces and metrics
Create Grafana dashboard and saved panels for the run (evictions, circuit states, kv-hit-rate, p50/p95/p99)
Add automated post-run report generator and S3/GDrive upload step
Run smoke tests in staging and iterate on thresholds
Document runbook steps and escalation paths; link to Confluence page
steps_to_run: 1. Provision a staging deployment spanning Region-A (primary) and Region-B (standby) with synthetic tenants (high/medium/low).
2. Enable harness: set chaos-run id and run config via /internal/chaos/run endpoint.
3. Start control-plane egress throttle to Region-A (simulate asymmetric partition) with 10s ramps.
4. Trigger GPU pool reclamation: call drain API with percent targets [30, 50, 70] over 10-minute windows.
5. Enable dependency proxy: inject 100-800ms jitter and 5xxs ramping from 1% to 25% over 15 minutes.
6. Observe admission controller logs and verify tenant-prioritized throttles; assert that high-priority tenants retain capacity where possible.
7. Verify circuit breaker transitions in tracing UI and confirm fallback model routing when circuit opens.
8. Collect metrics, traces, and post-run report; upload artifacts and open retrospective ticket with findings.
